set.body: Evidence: side-256 copy_inner_stride produced 262144 output bytes but allocated 1337708 B/op; copy_transpose produced 524288 output bytes but allocated 2648430 B/op, about 32 avoidable bytes per element from generic get/set and callback traversal. Implement dtype-dispatched materialization: bulk copy for canonical contiguous regions, monomorphic inner-stride loops, cache-tiled transpose loops, and a counter-based general fallback with no generic element dispatch. Route NDArray.copy and freeze/copy boundaries through it without changing ownership. Acceptance: JVM and Scala.js differential laws over adversarial layouts; result allocation no more than output buffer plus 2048 bytes; at least 10x speedup over the frozen baseline and at least 0.25x NumPy at both sizes; bytecode and optimized-JS proof of no per-element boxing or callbacks.
